# How can you get your sleep rhythm back after holiday travel and late parties, before the new year?

That question is now the first line of our own App Store listing: holiday travel, late parties or jet lag. We built Sleep Reset, listed on the App Store as For Better Sleep - Sleep Reset, for exactly this stretch of the year, when bedtimes drift later, mornings start at different hours, and a few disrupted nights turn into a schedule that no longer matches the day you need to live. I am writing this as the maker, from what the app actually does today and from our own measured App Store numbers, not from generic sleep advice.

The goal I set for this guide is modest and practical: start before the new year, while the drift is still recent, and start with a measurement instead of a resolution.

## Why does a holiday schedule drift so quickly?

A holiday week rarely breaks a sleep schedule in one night. It bends it a little at a time. A late party moves bedtime by an hour. A travel day moves it again, in the other direction. You sleep in to recover, which feels sensible that morning, and then you are not sleepy at your usual bedtime that night.

After a few days of that, the problem is no longer one short night. The problem is that your bedtime, your wake time, and your energy in the afternoon are all pointing at different schedules. Trying to fix all three at once, by willpower, is why most of my own attempts used to fail by the second evening.

That is why we do not start Sleep Reset with a plan. We start it with a score.

## How does the free sleep reset score work?

On our [Sleep Reset product page](/sleepreset), I describe the start plainly: answer the app's onboarding questions about your goals to get your free sleep reset score and recovery outlook.

The score and the recovery outlook are free. That matters to me, because the first step after a disrupted week should not require a purchase decision at the moment you feel worst. You answer the questions, you see where you stand, and you see the outlook before you decide anything else.

On the App Store listing, I say the same thing in one line: get your free sleep reset score in a minute, then start a 7-day free trial if you want the full reset. The trial is for the paid part. The score itself is the free starting point.

## What does the paid reset actually add?

A paid subscription unlocks the personalised reset plan, bedtime timing, and next-morning recovery steps. Guided breathwork, which you follow as a breathing count as part of your bedtime routine, also requires a paid subscription.

I keep that boundary explicit in the app and on the product page, because I do not want anyone to download Sleep Reset expecting the full plan to be free. Free: the score and the recovery outlook. Paid: the personalised plan, bedtime timing, guided breathwork, and next-morning recovery steps.

The current App Store listing shows Weekly at $7.99 and Yearly at $59.99, with a 7-day free trial mentioned in the listing text. Prices and trial terms can vary, so please review the price and renewal terms shown before you subscribe, and manage or cancel in your Apple ID subscription settings.

## How should you use the first evening back?

Here is the sequence I recommend, using only what the app actually offers.

First, take the score in daylight, not at 2am. Answer the onboarding questions about your goals honestly, including the late nights and the travel, because the recovery outlook is only useful if it starts from the week you actually had.

Second, read the recovery outlook before you change anything. The outlook is the point of the free step: it turns a vague feeling of being off schedule into a starting point you can act on that evening.

Third, if you continue, follow the bedtime timing in the personalised plan instead of inventing your own jump back to your old bedtime in one night. A reset plan exists precisely because a sudden, large correction is hard to hold.

Fourth, use the guided breathwork as part of the bedtime routine, following the breathing count, rather than scrolling until you feel tired. And the next morning, follow the next-morning recovery steps instead of improvising, because the morning after a late night is where the drift usually continues.

## Does Sleep Reset treat insomnia?

No. Sleep Reset is a general-wellness app, not medical advice, and it does not guarantee a particular sleep outcome. I state that on the product page, and I am stating it again here.

If sleep problems persist, or if you suspect a medical condition, please speak to a qualified clinician. This app is for recovering a disrupted schedule after travel, late parties, and jet lag, not for treating a disorder.

## What do our own numbers say, honestly?

I publish our measured numbers in these guides because I do not want to claim traction we do not have.

According to App Store Connect data measured on 22 November 2026 (file measured_at 2026-11-22T21:44:39Z), over the 28 days from 25 October to 21 November 2026, Sleep Reset recorded 357 impressions, 8 product page views, and 2 downloads, both downloads in the US and both from App Store search. Over the most recent 7 days in that file, 15 to 21 November 2026, it recorded 66 impressions, 4 product page views, and 0 downloads. As of 21 November 2026, the app had 0 active paid subscriptions.

Those are small numbers, and I am not dressing them up. They are why I write these guides: so that someone whose schedule has just drifted can find a free, one-minute starting point, and so that our own discovery improves honestly, one reader at a time.

## Which devices can you use?

Sleep Reset is listed for iPhone and requires iOS 18.0 or later. The App Store listing shows version 1.0.4, dated 12 November, at 11.3 MB, in English, in Health & Fitness, with Data Not Collected declared by the developer. That update removes the rating prompt from onboarding for a smoother first-run experience, and improves reliability.

You can read more on our [Sleep Reset product page](/sleepreset) and on the [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/for-better-sleep-sleep-reset/id6762143790).

## How is this different from waking up at 2am?

In my previous guide, [What can you do when you wake up at 2am after a night shift or jet lag?](/blog/sleep-reset-wake-at-2am-shift-jet-lag), I focused on a single bad night. This guide is about a pattern over several days: the holiday stretch, where travel and late parties move your rhythm gradually.

The starting point is the same free score. The difference is timing. If you take the score while the drift is still a few days old, before the new year, the reset you are asking for is smaller than the one you will need after another week of sleeping in.

For a calmer evening wind-down, some of our readers also use a single verse from [Daily Dhamma](/blog/c/daily-dhamma) before bed. That is a reading pause, not a sleep treatment, and I mention it only as a companion habit.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the sleep reset score really free?

Yes. The sleep reset score and recovery outlook are free. The personalised plan, bedtime timing, guided breathwork, and next-morning recovery steps require a separate paid subscription.

### How long does the score take?

Our App Store listing says you can get your free sleep reset score in a minute. You answer the onboarding questions about your goals, and the score and outlook follow from those answers.

### Is there a free trial?

The App Store listing text mentions a 7-day free trial for the paid reset. Please confirm the trial, price, and renewal terms shown for your account before you subscribe, because terms can vary.

### Can Sleep Reset fix jet lag overnight?

I make no such guarantee. Sleep Reset is a general-wellness app that helps you work through a disrupted schedule with a score, a plan, bedtime timing, breathwork, and morning steps. It does not guarantee a particular sleep outcome.

### Where can I see more Sleep Reset guides?

All of our Sleep Reset guides are collected on the [Sleep Reset category hub](/blog/c/sleep-reset), including our explainer [How does the sleep reset score work?](/blog/sleep-reset-score-explained).

Start with your score, while the holiday drift is still recent. That is the smallest honest first step I can offer you before the new year.
